newsitem.title: UK: N.American air cargo market to grow 5.5 pct yr.
newsitem.headline: N.American air cargo market to grow 5.5 pct yr.

text.p: Air cargo growth for the combined U.S. and Canadian markets is expected to be at annual average rate of 6.1 percent during the next 10 years, and 5.5 percent for the 20 years to 2015, Boeing Co said.
The U.S. domestic market will represent 26.7 percent of the world air cargo market by 2015 compared to last year's 31.7 percent, it added in its World Air Cargo forecast released here on Thursday.
Boeing said that revenue tonne kilometres (RTKS) for the U.S. market rose 5.5 percent in 1995 over the previous year, nearly double the 2.8 percent growth for the U.S. economy.
"This relationship indicates that the U.S. domestic air cargo industry is still not mature, since air cargo growth continues to outpace GDP growth."

It noted that the "express carriers experienced growth of 9.7 percent, thereby increasing their overall share of the market to 59.4 percent. Their share has moved up 15 percent since 1990." This " will continue to increase as manufacturers and shippers integrate more time-definite transportation into their operations, and as scheduled airlinesreduce the use of widebody aircraft on domestic services - effectively reducing the cargo capacity offered by airlines and forwarders,"Boeing added. The U.S.domestic market will continue to reprsent 90 percent of the North American market with growth rates of six percent a year over 10 years and 5.4 percent over 20 years. For the Canadian market these rates are 4.1 percent and 3.9 percent respectively, it said. Air cargo trade between Latin America and North America is forecast to rise at an annual average of 6.5 percent over the 20 years, despite a moderate growth of 3.7 percent in 1995, Boeing added.

However since 1990, the overall market has grown by 47 percent ,with foreign investment, low interest rates and intraregional trade spurring Latin American growth , it said. "Demand for Latin American products continues to grow in North America. Development and the potential expansion of the North American Free Trade Area could also result in the relocation of manufacturing activities from other parts of the world, fuelling this growth,"it added. Growth in both northbound and southbound trade has continued to expand as the breadth of goods continues to widen. Northbound trade is dominated by flowers and fish, although their share is slowly declining, while southbound trade is led by office equipment and other machinery. But the continued growth in the air cargo market will result in some direct services bypassing Miami.
